clue.text: Actor in dance not turning his head

indicators.note: the actor's pieces sit in the dance, so the dance word is opened up to take them

parts.note: the Charleston is a 1920s dance

indicators.note: turning signals that the word not is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round

indicators.note: the head of his is its first letter

explanation.surface: A performer who dances while keeping his head perfectly still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor in dance' suggests a dancing actor, but 'in' is the container signal: 'turning' reverses NOT, and with the first letter of 'his' this sits inside the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlton Heston was the Hollywood star of Ben-Hur and The Ten Commandments.

clue.text: Retreat from island? it takes a long time

parts.note: Herm is one of the smaller Channel Islands
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A getaway from an island that takes ages to reach.
explanation.walkthrough: HERM is a small Channel Island near Guernsey; the question mark marks the playful split of the definition from the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermitage is a secluded dwelling, a place of withdrawal from the world.

clue.text: Dance tune that's odd with only two band members

parts.note: rum is an informal British word for strange or odd

indicators.note: with only two of its members kept, the word band loses its last letters

parts.note: the word band, cut down to its first pair

explanation.surface: A strange melody played by a group reduced to a duo.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM means odd in British slang; 'with only two' keeps BA of BAND, dropping ND.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance and the music played for it.

clue.text: No stimulating!

parts.note: read as an instruction, turning the letters of on gives the clue's word No

explanation.surface: A flat refusal that is somehow also exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, tells you to turn ON round, which produces NO, the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that excites or arouses someone is said to be getting them going in that way.

clue.text: Suitable position for hotel in French resort

indicators.note: in signals that the hotel letter goes inside the resort name

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the Riviera
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Finding the right spot for a hotel on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a place or role that fits someone well.

clue.text: Having abandoned Hendon, I've a place in the Netherlands

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so the letters run loose

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone has left a London suburb for a Dutch town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hendon is a suburb of north London; 'abandoned' looks like leaving it but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eindhoven is a city in the south of the Netherlands, home of Philips.

clue.text: Material that's precious, associated with diamonds

parts.note: precious in the sense of affectedly dainty means twee
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A fabric so valuable it is mentioned alongside gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precious' suggests value but means twee (affectedly quaint).
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen cloth.

clue.text: Island overturning 50 per cent of vote, demanding recount

indicators.note: overturning signals that the island's name is read backwards

parts.note: Arran is a Scottish island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: half of the four letters of vote, here the back half

explanation.surface: Islanders overturn half the vote and call for another count.
explanation.walkthrough: ARRAN backwards gives NARRA; '50 per cent of' takes TE, the second half of VOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount is to tell a story, to relate events in order.

clue.text: A hero's at sea but not at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hero is away on a voyage, yet paradoxically on land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' is used twice: first as the anagram signal (confused), then literally in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on land rather than on the water is the opposite of being afloat.

clue.text: Bearing stuff on your bike!

parts.note: S, south, is a compass bearing
to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: Loading things onto your bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On your bike!' is a British way of telling someone to go away; it is not about cycling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are brusque commands to leave immediately.

clue.text: Freak or centaur — one with interesting relations

indicators.note: freak hints at something abnormal, so the letters are distorted

explanation.surface: A monster or a mythical half-horse whose family is fascinating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' looks like family but means accounts or stories told.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled storyteller, and a relation is a narrative.

clue.text: Craft seen in the morning — about dawn, mostly

indicators.note: about has the shortened dawn word placed round the morning letters
mostly signals that the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a dawn is a beginning or origin
AM means in the morning

explanation.surface: A boat spotted early, around sunrise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ORIGIN to ORIGI, which goes about AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese craft of folding paper.

clue.text: An animal can hide round the bend

indicators.note: round the bend means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A creature that can conceal itself around a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round the bend' looks like a place but is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna is a spiny egg-laying mammal of Australia.

clue.text: Excise backing Caesarean section

indicators.note: backing means the extracted run is read in the reverse direction
a section of the word Caesarean is taken out of it

explanation.surface: A surgeon removes something in a Caesarean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'section' takes ESARE from inside CaESAREan; 'backing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to cut out, to delete or remove.

clue.text: Pure as the rolling river

indicators.note: rolling suggests movement, so the letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A river as clean as it is rolling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Euphrates is a great river of the Middle East.

clue.text: Wilder girls in 1953 road movie?

parts.note: Gene Wilder was an American comic actor
Vi is a girl's name
Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Female characters in a Billy Wilder-style film of the early fifties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilder' looks like the comparative of wild, or the director Billy Wilder, but is actor Gene Wilder.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1953 British comedy follows a vintage car in the London to Brighton rally.

clue.text: Wind putting end to celebration or festival

indicators.note: the end of celebration is its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
Easter is a Christian festival

explanation.surface: A gust that stops a party or holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong storm blowing from the north-east, especially on the US Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Holding out, nuts madden attendants

indicators.note: holding means the anger word has the other letters inside it

parts.note: to madden is to enrage

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: Crazy holdouts drive the staff mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding out' reads like a holdout, but 'Holding' is the container signal and 'nuts' scrambles the word out.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is a group of people accompanying an important person.

clue.text: E revealing experience?

explanation.surface: A letter that teaches something new.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter E opens the word 'eye', hence an opener of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter starts the word for the organ of sight; and a surprising experience shows you something new.

clue.text: Saying nothing about a Rolls-Royce being taken back is a mistake

indicators.note: being taken back means the whole assembly is read backwards
about places the silent word around the car letters

parts.note: someone saying nothing is mute

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about returning a Rolls-Royce is an error.
explanation.walkthrough: MUTE about A RR gives MUTARRE; 'being taken back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in print or writing.

clue.text: Fool about with explosive ingredient

parts.note: nit is British slang for a fool
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An idiot messing about with explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: NIT is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is a component of gunpowder.

clue.text: Gas more than electricity? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the phrase is used, a run from inside it

explanation.surface: Is gas better than electric?
explanation.definitionFit: Ethane is a colourless hydrocarbon, a component of natural gas.

clue.text: Rider from Boston to Concord ultimately esteemed

parts.note: Paul Revere made the famous midnight ride in 1775

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of Concord

explanation.surface: A historic rider honoured at the end of his journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Revere rode from Boston toward Concord to warn of British troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Revered means deeply respected.

clue.text: One with restricted diet, say, boarding vehicle

indicators.note: boarding means getting into the vehicle, so letters go inside it

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
EG, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A fussy eater gets on a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan eats no animal products.

clue.text: Fool accepting large double

indicators.note: accepting means the fool word takes the size letter in

parts.note: to dupe is to fool

explanation.surface: A fool takes on a big double.
explanation.definitionFit: Duple means twofold, as in duple time in music.

clue.text: If necessary, put a cuckoo in a tree

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters go inside the tree

parts.note: the ash is a tree

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Place a cuckoo in a tree if you must.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuckoo' looks like the bird but signals the letters of PUT A becoming TAPU.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in an emergency, when needed.

clue.text: Attic starter

parts.note: Attic means of ancient Athens, so this is the opening letter of the Greek letter sequence, not something in a loft

explanation.definitionFit: Attic is classical Greek, and the first of its letters is the one before beta.

clue.text: Pickled? See pickle

parts.note: pickled and tight both mean drunk
to spot is to see

explanation.surface: A drunk asked to look at a jar of preserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickled' and 'pickle' look like the same idea but are drunk and a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickle is a predicament, an awkward situation.

clue.text: Frank is not attractive

explanation.definitionFit: Plain means honest and direct, and also unattractive or homely.

clue.text: Cook was rather mean about unknown bird

indicators.note: about means the cooked letters surround the unknown
to cook is to doctor or rearrange

parts.note: X is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A chef was rather stingy with a mysterious ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a chef but signals the anagram of WAS RATHER MEAN, which goes about X.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manx shearwater is a seabird of the North Atlantic.
